deviations.what: the model casts floating inputs (latents, text embeddings, pooled embedding, audio latents) to its dtype; the timestep stays as given
deviations.why: torch raises on a dtype mismatch, but MLX silently promotes a float32 input against bf16 weights and would run the whole model in float32. In float32 the cast is a no-op.

deviations.what: returns a tuple (video,) or (video, audio), like the reference with return_dict=False; there is no output dataclass
deviations.why: the pipeline (spec 09) is the only caller

deviations.what: stage B inputs: text embeddings computed from the study notebook's Smoke prompt with the pipeline's own encode_prompt (padded to 1024 tokens with the boolean mask) instead of the notebook's cache
deviations.why: the notebook's output holds no cached embeddings, and its cache drops the padding; keeping the mask exercises the masked path the pipeline uses.

architecture_notes.note: Measured forward: 1.45 s at Smoke, 76 s at Baseline (peak 8.05 / 11.6 GiB); the sum of profiled blocks predicts 1.45 s and 71.9 s (scripts/profile_components.py (real Lite-distill weights, bf16, M3 Max, 2026-10-31)). 10 Baseline steps are about 12.7 min on DiT alone.
architecture_notes.optimization: Baseline is attention bound; Smoke has room for mx.compile and fusion.

architecture_notes.topic: text padding is wasted work and removable exactly
architecture_notes.note: The pipeline pads the prompt to 1024 tokens with a mask (about 200 valid for the Smoke prompt). Masked keys get zero weight and padded queries never influence other tokens, so dropping the padding before the model changes outputs only by summation order: rel_max 1.5e-6 (video) and 2.3e-6 (audio) on the real model in float32 at Smoke. Saves 4 text blocks x (9.0 -> 2.6 ms) and 32 x (6.9 -> 4.5 ms) cross-attention: about 7% at Smoke, about 1% at Baseline.
architecture_notes.optimization: Trim padded text (right padding keeps RoPE positions) in the MLX pipeline (spec 09/14); keep the masked path for parity tests.

architecture_notes.note: Video and audio RoPE tables, the text input projections (video/audio_text_embeddings) and the per-step modulation vectors depend only on the prompt, the grid and the timestep, not on the latents; the text encoder blocks depend on the timestep through their modulation and must run every step.
architecture_notes.optimization: Cache RoPE tables and text projections for the whole generation; precompute all steps' modulation vectors and free the 2.2 GB of float32 modulation weights.

architecture_notes.note: The whole 32-block forward is built lazily and evaluated once; peak memory is set by the largest block activations (Baseline 11.6 GiB including 6.4 GB of weights + 2.2 GB float32 modulation).
architecture_notes.optimization: Evaluate per block if memory gets tight (spec 14); mx.compile on a block function is the next experiment.
